__doc__: SOT-1459 per-role worker assignment. Editable file (NOT .env). Each harness role maps to an ORDERED PRIORITY CHAIN of workers: index 0 = primary (tried first), the rest = fallback order tried on non-response / usage-limit. Valid roles: task-check | decomposition | implementation | verification | acceptance | github | linear-report. Valid workers: claude | codex | antigravity. A bare string is accepted as a single-element chain (backward compatible). The dispatcher scripts/ai/run_worker.sh <role> reads this chain and invokes each worker's run script (run_codex.sh / run_claude.sh / run_antigravity.sh) in order: if a worker is non-responsive (exit 75) or hits its usage limit, the dispatcher hands off to the NEXT worker in the chain, passing the partial report so work continues. Consecutive invocations of the SAME worker reuse that CLI's session so the conversation/prompt cache stays warm. The former global env kill-switches (ALL_CLAUDE_MODE, WORKER_MODE) have been removed; this file is the single top-level worker selector. The per-worker availability flags (CODEX_DISABLED / ANTIGRAVITY_DISABLED / CLAUDE_DISABLED) and usage-limit cooldown are evaluated per worker, after chain selection. This file is the DEFAULT; a Linear issue can override roles for its own pipeline run with a directive line 'workers: role=worker[>fallback], ...' in its description or a comment (see src/lib/workerRoleDirective.ts and runner-cli resolve-worker-roles). Keys starting with __ are ignored. SOT-1569 (default worker policy): every role's static chain has primary=claude, secondary=codex, tertiary=antigravity (per human directive). SOT-1558 (doer/checker separation) previously set the verification/acceptance chains with a codex primary, then a DYNAMIC variant moved the implementation worker to the BACK of the acceptance chain; both have been REMOVED (per human directive: the dynamic separation that demoted the implementation worker on the acceptance chain is unnecessary), so acceptance/verification now resolve to the same static chain as every other role with no reordering. The SOT-1555 NOT_REQUIRED pin (PIPELINE_PINNED_WORKER) is unaffected: it keeps a non-code task (DOC/REVIEW/PLAN/QUESTION/SECURITY-scan) on ONE AI by moving the pinned worker to the FRONT of its chain. SOT-1583 (model selection): a per-issue directive may pin a MODEL per worker as 'workers: role=worker:model[>worker:model], ...' (e.g. implementation=codex:gpt-5.5, verification=claude:sonnet). The model is everything after the first colon (ids with dots/spaces/parens are kept verbatim); a missing model uses the worker's default. resolve-worker-roles records these pins under a __models__ section of the per-issue worker_roles.<issue>.json; the dispatcher run_worker.sh passes the selected worker's model via CODEX_MODEL (codex exec -m) / AGY_MODEL (agy --model) / CLAUDE_MODEL (claude --model, default opus). The base config may define default model pins under __models__; per-issue directives override them.
__solo_doc__: SOT-1591 SOLO MODE. When __solo__ is set to a single worker (claude | codex | antigravity), that ONE AI runs the ENTIRE issue lifecycle — task-check (incl. decomposition judgment) → implementation → verification → acceptance → github (branch/PR/merge) → linear-report — in ONE dispatch / one CLI session, with NO per-role script handoff or gating in between (run_auto.sh does a single 'run_worker.sh solo' dispatch instead of looping roles). This is the 'run everything on one AI, no script relay' mode. The per-role priority chains below are IGNORED while __solo__ is active. EMPTY / BLANK BEHAVIOUR: __solo__ set to "" (blank), null, a missing key, or any value that is NOT one of claude|codex|antigravity ⇒ SOLO MODE OFF ⇒ the NORMAL per-role priority-chain pipeline below runs. Solo mode is ON only when __solo__ is exactly one of those three worker names. PER-ISSUE OVERRIDE (SOT-1591): a Linear directive line can flip solo mode for one issue — 'workers: solo=<worker>[:model]' forces solo on that worker (overriding this __solo__), and 'workers: solo=off' forces the normal per-role pipeline for that issue; parser src/lib/workerRoleDirective.ts, applied by runner-cli resolve-worker-roles. HANDOFF: solo still uses one AI at a time for the entire lifecycle; with __handoff__=true, an unavailable solo worker hands the entire lifecycle to the next worker. __handoff__=false keeps solo strictly on the selected worker. Resolver: src/lib/workerRoles.ts resolveSoloWorker/loadSoloWorker; CLI: runner-cli solo-worker.
__handoff_doc__: Cross-worker handoff policy. true (default) allows the dispatcher to try the next worker in each role chain after a failure. A Linear issue may override this with workers: handoff=off or workers: handoff=on.
